summary: Superior National Forest lookout near Ely in what is now the Boundary Waters wilderness; listed as gone, but a 2009 hike account says most of the old tower remains.

facts.design: square-cab tower (the second lookout on the site)
facts.status_note: Listed as gone by the Forest Fire Lookout Association; a 2009 hike account says most of the old tower remains on site

access.note: Inside the Boundary Waters Canoe Area Wilderness and reached on foot; no current access rules found in the sources read

visit.trail_note: About six miles on foot per the 2009 account; the spur to the site is reclaimed by forest, so GPS is needed to find the remains

events.note: First tower on the site, based on forest guard records; the county list prints 1912 and 1913 beside it with no labels, so the build year is not confirmed (1912 is the earlier printed year)
Second lookout, a square-cab tower; the county list says it probably dates to the mid-1920s, so the year is approximate
Photo caption shows guards at the lookout cabin, August 1932

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The county list prints both 1912 and 1913 beside the first tower with no labels, so neither is confirmed as the build year. The event keeps 1912 only as the earlier printed year, marked as other, and the story names no build year.

notes_for_editor: The only description of the site today is a 2009 hike account, which says most of the old tower remains. It conflicts with the FFLA 'Tower Gone' entry; both are reported and status stays gone with that caveat. The 1952 survey note and the 2004 removal note in the St. Louis County list belong to Skibo, not Sioux River. The Forest Service Fire and Ice page describes a different Sioux fire overlook on the Echo Trail, and no source read links it to this tower. The 1932 photo is credited to the Forest History Society in the account, but no image URL was found, so no photo entry. Wilderness access rules were not checked against a current Forest Service source.
